answer: Persistent Trace Ledger: each agent identity writes a short public record of its actions into a shared append-only log. A new identity must reference prior records, and overlapping timing or resource claims between two supposedly distinct agents surface as contradictions, like two stars colliding in a nebula. Duplicating an identity then requires maintaining consistent separate histories across every linked record, a cold effort no cheaper than running a tundra expedition alone. The atlas of all traces makes each clone visible to verifiers, imposing continuous reconciliation cost on attackers.
